title: Upgrade kernellib and rewrite lifecycle adapters for GPU telemetry
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Upgrade the internal kernel selection library (kernellib) to v4.2 and refactor the node lifecycle adapters to a non-blocking v2 interface that emits standardized GPU telemetry events.

Why: kernellib v4.x contains critical optimizations (batched kernel dispatch, adaptive shared-memory tiling) that materially reduce per-token CPU overhead on mixed workloads. The current lifecycle adapters perform synchronous health probes and blocking reconciliation calls that add tail latency during pod reprovisioning and autoscaler cycles. Moving to an evented lifecycle adapter reduces blocking on the autoscaler reconciliation path and centralizes telemetry emission for downstream observability.

Goals:
- Upgrade kernellib to 4.2 across runtime packages and validate ABI compatibility.
- Replace blocking lifecycle adapters with a v2 evented adapter that writes standardized GPU lifecycle/telemetry events to the fleet event bus.
- Introduce a short compatibility shim so older Dedicated controllers can read events during rollout.
- Measure p50/p95/p99 latency and reconcile-loop duration pre/post-change; target 20% reduction in p99 reconcile latency and <=5% CPU uplift overall.

Scope:
- Code: runtime/kernelshim, autoscaler/lifecycle-adapters, observability/event-schema.
- Tests: unit, integration (simulated scale-up/scale-down), e2e in staging with full overlay.
- Ops: canary rollout across one region (eu-west-1) then global.

Non-goals: rewriting capacity planner logic or autoscaler algorithm. This is an infrastructural refactor aimed at decoupling telemetry and lifecycle side-effects from the critical path.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Incompatible kernellib ABI: keep a temporary dual-abi build and run runtime unit tests and perf harnesses; gating on green before rolling.
- Event loss during early rollout: buffer events in sidecar and enable durable delivery to event bus; replay mechanism for missed lifecycle events.
- Regressed reconcile latency due to excessive event processing: offload processing to async worker pools and maintain backpressure metrics.

Testing Plan:
- Microbench: run kernellib v4.2 perf harness against standard model suites (gpt-medium, llama-13b) and compare token throughput and CPU utilization.
- Integration: deploy lifecycle-adapter-v2 to staging with simulated node churn (scale test) and validate reconcile duration and autoscaler stability.
- Observability: add temporary dashboards for event throughput, event lag, reconcile duration, and p99 serving latency.

Rollout Plan:
1) Merge kernellib upgrade behind feature flag and run CI perf jobs.
2) Deploy lifecycle-adapter-v2 to staging with compatibility shim enabled.
3) Canary: enable in eu-west-1 (10% of fleet) for 48h; monitor reconcile duration, p99, and error rates.
4) Progressive rollout to other regions with automated rollback threshold (reconcile p99 > baseline * 1.2 or error spike > 5x).

Follow-ups:
- Add long-term backlog item to remove compatibility shim after 2 sprints.
- Proposal to extend event schema for richer KV cache diagnostics.

- Perf PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Integration PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/2140
comments: 2026-02-22 — Initial spike completed: kernellib upgrade builds successfully in bazel; one ABI break in runtime/cuda-ops shim discovered (fixed with wrapper). Next: add perf harness runs for gpt-medium.
2026-02-28 — Design review (pm + infra): agreed on event schema and compatibility shim approach. Action: Diego to protoype sidecar buffering and replay logic.
2026-03-04 — Perf baseline: staging run shows kernellib v4.2 improves avg kernel dispatch time by ~12% and reduces CPU sys by ~7% on our mixed batch traces. Will include results in PR.
2026-03-08 — PR opened for lifecycle-adapter-v2: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/2140 — awaiting eng review (requested reviewers: @maria_chen, @oliver_khan).

2026-03-10 — Integration test: simulated scale-up in staging (200 node churn) shows reconcile p99 reduced from 380ms to 295ms with adapter-v2 and sidecar buffering enabled. Noted a small increase (~3%) in event bus lag during spikes; added backpressure metrics and worker autoscaling.
2026-03-12 — Security review: IAM for event bus topics scoped; no secrets introduced. Security review flagged durable replay storage encryption; added KMS integration task.
